One classification changes four things: the application, the evidence, the arrears calculation, and the collection process. Ontario's

Consider two units with similar winter electricity use.
Fixed monthly charge:

Unit 4's lease requires an $80 utility payment to the landlord each month. Because the amount is fixed, it meets the definition of rent. The rent ledger and lease clause should show the charge consistently.

Documenting Charges So They Hold Up at the Board

A clean meter read still fails if nobody can match it to the lease and the rule that allows the charge. Unresolved disputes at the Landlord and Tenant Board sit for months. The file has to be auditable on the day you bill, not the week before a hearing.

Classification comes first. A utility payment is either rent or it is not rent. That split decides which application fits, what evidence the member will expect, and how arrears are calculated. Billing records have to match the classification before anyone pursues the charge. An electricity line the lease calls a separate commodity is not the same thing as a fixed amount the lease calls rent, even when the dollar figure looks identical. Ontario's residential tenancy rules draw that line. Other provinces use their own boards and tests, so do not carry an Ontario file structure into a hearing somewhere else without checking the local rule.

The invoice works like a grocery receipt. One blended total hides which item the lease allows. Split consumption, pass-through charges, taxes, and late-payment penalties on the tenant invoice and on the owner's ledger. Delivery, regulatory, debt-retirement, billing, administrative, tax, setup, and late-payment charges can all appear on an electricity bill. If they sit inside one number, nobody can test which part the clause permits.

Tenancy clause:
the sentence that creates the duty, quoted, not paraphrased.
Classification:
rent, or a charge outside rent, in the same words as the lease.
Utility rule:
suite meter, shared allocation, or a fixed amount that is rent.
Meter identifier:
the unit meter, not the building bulk meter.
Billing period:
start and end dates that do not overlap the previous invoice.
Opening and closing reads:
actual figures, with any estimated read labelled as estimated.
Adjustments:
credits, rebills, and the reason for each.
The property audit file

Keep, in one folder per building, the signed agreement, baseline utility data, the allocation formula, the effective-date notice, the rent-reduction calculation, and proof of what you sent the tenant. We may disclose customer, unit, and account information, including consumption, allocation, and payment information, to the landlord, property manager, developer, condominium corporation, or owner, and the customer consents to that. What the Landlord and Tenant Board Does

The Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB) is Ontario's tribunal for residential landlord and tenant disputes under the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006. Its modern role dates to 1998, when this work moved out of the provincial courts. Say a manager in a mid-rise has a tenant who has ignored a hydro share since March. The manager doesn't open a small-claims file. Rent, maintenance, termination, possession, and related tenancy obligations are heard here, and a utility disagreement usually rides inside one of those applications rather than as a standalone utility claim.

The hearing load

Tribunals Ontario recorded 89,494 in-person, electronic, and written hearing events during fiscal year 2024–2025 on its LTB key performance indicators. Landlord files, including non-profit housing co-operative applications, make up the bulk of that work. Tenant files are the smaller share, and that split has held since the court transfer.

Learn the forum before you pursue any charge. The form and the charge setup come after you know who actually decides the dispute.

One classification changes four things: the application, the evidence, the arrears calculation, and the collection process. Ontario's L1 instructions distinguish a tenant's obligation to pay a share of a utility bill from a fixed monthly utility payment made to the landlord.

A tenant's obligation to pay all or part of a hydro bill, directly to the utility or indirectly through the landlord, is not rent. A fixed monthly utility amount paid to the landlord meets the definition of rent.

Hearing. The board hears the matter in person, electronically, or in writing. It applies the rent or non-rent classification to decide the amount. A precise read doesn't rescue a charge pursued on the wrong basis.

Order. The result is a board order. Recovery tracks the amounts established at the hearing, not the total you typed on the form.

While the claim waits, landlords should keep essential services running. Tenants should keep paying every amount that isn't in dispute. Bring the lease, the notices, the audit file, and the written correction. If the correction already did the work, you may not need the hearing at all.
